rules.description: Expression used as statement with no effect — e.g. a variable name on its own line. GDScript 4 emits 'Expression is not assigned to a variable' or parse error depending on context.
GDScript 4 requires colon after if/elif/else/for/while/func/class. GDScript 3 allowed some omissions. Migration scripts may drop colons.
GDScript 3 used 'export var x'. GDScript 4 uses '@export var x'. The old form causes parse error in Godot 4.
GDScript 3 used 'onready var x'. GDScript 4 uses '@onready var x'. The old form causes parse error.
GDScript 3 used node.connect('signal', target, 'method'). GDScript 4 uses node.signal.connect(callable). Old syntax causes TypeError at runtime.
GDScript 3 used yield(). GDScript 4 removed yield() — use await instead. yield() causes parse error in GDScript 4.

A variable is referenced in a function scope where it was not declared and is not a class member. In GDScript 4 this causes 'Identifier not found' parse error. Confirmed: Document 1 lines 2049/2052/2056 reference `plane` inside _find_node_with_method() where plane is only in scope in _create_plane().
Two scripts declare the same class_name. GDScript 4 emits 'Class already defined' parse error.
Return type annotation uses a type not yet registered at parse time. GDScript 4 is strict about forward references in type annotations.
GDScript 3 used 'tool' keyword at top of file. GDScript 4 uses '@tool' annotation. Old form causes parse error.
GDScript 3 used 'var x setget setter,getter'. GDScript 4 uses property with get/set blocks. Old form causes parse error.
GDScript 3 used 'signal my_signal(arg)'. GDScript 4 uses 'signal my_signal(arg: Type)'. Untyped signal args may cause warnings or errors.
GDScript 3 used $Node/Path shorthand without quotes. Some paths with special characters require NodePath() in GDScript 4.
An annotation (@export, @onready, @tool) appears outside its valid scope — e.g. inside a function body. GDScript 4 emits parse error.

Code appears after a `return` statement in the same scope, making it unreachable. GDScript 4 does not raise a parse error for this but the UNREACHABLE_CODE warning is emitted. When the unreachable code also references out-of-scope variables (VR007), gdparse reports those as errors. Confirmed: Document 1 lines 2045-2056 in scope _find_node_with_method were unreachable after `return null` at line 2044. The VR007 violations at 2049/2052/2056 were inside this dead-code block.

Signal declared in emitter node but connect() never called in host script. GDScript 4 does not error on unconnected signals — the game runs but signal fires into void. Confirmed: jumped_from_plane declared in plane.gd, connect() was only in dead-code block (lines 2045-2056, after return null), removed by F18. Signal was disconnected before and after F18.
Called but no func definition in any scanned .gd file — runtime crash if reached.
Defined but never called from any scanned .gd file — dead code candidate.
Signal declared but no .connect() in any .gd or [connection] in any .tscn.

	# AUTO-GENERATED by generate_fix_0227.py
	# WHAT: connect landed signal — deferred for load-order safety
	# WHY: direct connect() in _ready() fails if receiver not yet in tree.
	#   Deferred call runs after current frame, by which time all
	#   autoloaded and scene-tree nodes are available.
	# MENTAL MODEL BEFORE: landed fires into void (VR019 liveness violation)
	# MENTAL MODEL AFTER: landed -> receiver._on_landed()
	# FAILURE MODE: if no node has _on_landed(), warning printed;
	#   game continues without crash.
	# VERIFIES WITH: '[VERBATIM] landed connected OK' in Godot log
	# Source (Tier 1): Lamport (1994) ACM TOPLAS 16(3) p.872 — liveness
	#   https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/177492.177726
	# Source (Tier 2): call_deferred():
	#   https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_object.html
	# Source (Tier 2): Signal.connect():
	#   https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_signal.html
	# Source (Tier 1): Gamma et al. (1994) Ch.5 p.315 — Observer pattern
	call_deferred("_connect_landed")

	func _connect_landed() -> void:
		# WHAT: runtime connect for landed — called deferred from _ready
		# Source (Tier 2): Node.find_child():
		#   https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_node.html
		var _receiver = get_tree().get_root().find_child(
			"*", true, false
		)
		# Find first node with the receiver method
		var _nodes = get_tree().get_root().find_children("*", "", true, false)
		for _node in _nodes:
			if _node.has_method("_on_landed"):
				landed.connect(_node._on_landed)
				print("[VERBATIM] landed connected OK -> ",
					_node.name)
				return
		print("[VERBATIM] WARNING: no receiver for landed found")
